newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd group says it now holds northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kurd group says it now holds northern Iraq.

text.p: A Kurdish militia allied to Baghdad said on Monday that it controlled the whole of northern Iraq after several weeks of clashes with a rival Kurdish group.

"The (Kurdistan Democratic Party) KDP is in control of all the three Kurdish provinces," the KDP said in a statement. It said an armed feud with Jalal Talabani's Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) had ended with the KDP's seizure of a key city earlier on Monday.
"The bitter and tragic episode that was caused by the fratricidal war imposed unreasonably by Talabani's PUK in their quest for total hegemony is finally over," it said.
The KDP of Massoud Barzani earlier in the day captured the city of Sulaimaniya, Iraqi Kurdistan's biggest city and the PUK's main stronghold.
Fighting between the factions broke out last month, shattering a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
Washington launched punitive missile attacks on southern Iraq after tens of thousands of government troops helped the KDP capture the city of Arbil on August 31.
